recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Handle future doseAndRate.type binding-target or binding-strength work under the later binding-specific Jira issues rather than reopening this cardinality and missing-meaning seed.
issue_request: FHIR-19485 was Published/Persuasive for Pharmacy. It objected that Dosage.doseAndRate.type was mandatory while using a wide-open CodeableConcept/example binding, and resolved to make the element 0..1 with ordered as the meaning if missing rather than a real default.
initial_application: Jira links merge commit 7a787c5ab6b278c2af6d3644c38931486b7330f4. Its GF 19485 source commit 5262ee548c7b86f38e88093b6be05706be6b3d49 changed source/datatypes/dosage.xml for Dosage.doseAndRate.type from 1..1 to 0..1 and added the ordered-if-missing guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps Dosage in current build scope as an active datatype/page owned by Pharmacy and marked normative. Current source/datatypes/dosage.xml still has cardinality 0..1, CodeableConcept, DoseAndRateType, and the ordered-if-missing comment. Later same-area Jira context does not reverse the seed: FHIR-34129 declined changing the binding to required, and FHIR-40217 concerned the binding target rather than the cardinality/missing-meaning rule. Direct FHIR-19485 community searches found no contrary Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit only. No source edit is needed because the current authoritative source already represents FHIR-19485's required semantic change.
